On 21 December 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2719 at meeting S/PV.9518 on financing for African Union-led peace support operations. The Council agreed to consider requests from the African Union Peace and Security Council case by case. Authorized operations would remain under African Union command and control. For operations authorized by the Council, UN assessed contributions may cover up to 75 percent of the annual operation budget. The UN and African Union are to jointly mobilize the remainder as extrabudgetary resources. The Council committed to consider viable options if significant shortfalls arise.

At S/PV.9518, the Council voted on the US amendment S/2023/1023, which passed with nine votes in favor, none against, and six abstentions including France. The amended draft S/2023/999 subsequently passed unanimously with 15 votes in favor, leading to the adoption of Resolution 2719. The US requested an explicit contribution limit to remove ambiguity regarding UN financing, clarifying that full UN funding was excluded. France abstained on the amendment due to insufficient clarity on financing the 25 percent outside assessed contributions, seeking predictability. While the Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2719, France reaffirmed support for assessed UN financing and prepared to discuss varying contribution levels with the EU, distinguishing its stance from the US push for explicit limits. The resolution authorized operations under African Union command, allowing UN assessed contributions to cover up to 75 percent of the budget, with the remainder to be mobilized as extrabudgetary resources. The Council committed to consider viable options if significant shortfalls arise. Uncertainty remains regarding the specific mechanisms for the EU's varying contribution levels.

solo.record:
On 21 December 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2719 at meeting S/PV.9518 on financing for African Union-led peace support operations. The Council agreed to consider requests from the African Union Peace and Security Council case by case. Authorized operations would remain under African Union command and control. For operations authorized by the Council, UN assessed contributions may cover up to 75 percent of the annual operation budget. The UN and African Union are to jointly mobilize the remainder as extrabudgetary resources. The Council committed to consider viable options if significant shortfalls arise.

At S/PV.9518, the US proposed an amendment to clarify financing limits, seeking an explicit cap to remove ambiguity and enable timely deployment. France abstained on this amendment, citing insufficient clarity regarding the 25 percent outside assessed contributions. Despite these dissenting views, the amendment passed with nine votes in favor and six abstentions, including France. The amended draft subsequently passed unanimously. The Council agreed to consider AU requests case-by-case, ensuring UN assessed contributions cover up to 75 percent of budgets, with the remainder mobilized jointly as extrabudgetary resources. While France expressed concern over the initial proposal's clarity, the final resolution confirmed the 75 percent cap. Uncertainty remains regarding the specific mobilization mechanisms for the remaining 25 percent, though the Council committed to considering viable options if significant shortfalls arise. The distinction between the amendment vote and the final unanimous adoption highlights the Council's ability to refine proposals while maintaining broad consensus on core financing principles.
